sheets.context_boundary: Each specialist runs in its own context window and returns a summary to the main conversation, which is the only place the chain is stitched together. The handoff is whatever the main session restates into the next prompt, so the finder's raw evidence does not reach the fixer unless it is carried forward explicitly; the shared files on disk are the other channel.
sheets.lifecycle: Each subagent starts when the main session delegates to it and ends when it returns its summary, with finished ones listed in /tasks. The chain stops after the verifier reports, and nothing persists between steps except the edited files and the main conversation.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open, and the lossy handoff is the real risk: the fixer sees only the finder's summary, so 'fix exactly what was found' can drift, and the verifier can confirm the summary rather than the code. Because all three touch the same hot files, any decision to overlap steps causes overwrites, and the documented isolation answer, worktrees, is unusable here since each step must see the previous step's edits.
sheets.version_caveat: Subagents are generally available with no enabling flag, experimental status or plan gate. The relevant change is tooling: as of v2.1.198 /agents no longer opens a panel and only prints subagent file locations, so the three definitions are created by asking Claude or editing the files directly.

sheets.primary: A dynamic workflow, or failing that a skill that defines a strict three stage chain, invoking three specialized subagents in sequence (finder, fixer, verifier) with each stage's structured output as the next stage's declared input. The sequencing belongs to the pipeline definition, not to a per-step model decision.
sheets.rejected_alternative: An agent team running the three specialists concurrently. Rejected because they all operate on the same handful of hot files, so concurrent edits would collide, and the dependency is genuinely serial: the fixer cannot start before the finder finishes.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness if a workflow or driver script executes the stages and passes the artifacts. The model if the chain is only described in a skill, which is materially weaker: a single model asked to do all three roles will tend to collapse them into one pass and verify its own work.
sheets.context_boundary: Three separate subagent contexts. What crosses each boundary is a structured handoff, first the finding list, then the change list or diff. The orchestrator retains only the handoffs, not the analysis transcripts, which is what keeps a long profiling session out of the main window.
sheets.lifecycle: Triggered once per performance pass and ends when the verifier reports. No stage persists, and the pipeline places no standing constraint on later edits to the same hot files.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open, and the lossy handoff is the practical failure: the fixer knows only what the finder wrote down, so it fixes the description rather than the issue, and the verifier then confirms the same description. Serial execution also buys no wall-clock saving, only role separation, and a verifier that can see the fixer's reasoning is a much weaker check than an independent one.
sheets.version_caveat: I am not confident about the current status or file format of the dynamic-workflow mechanism, so a skill defined chain is the version safe form of this answer. Sequential subagent invocation itself is generally available. I also do not know whether a subagent can dispatch the next stage itself or whether the chain must be driven from the parent.

sheets.primary: Subagents chained inside one session: three definitions under .claude/agents/ (a read-only performance finder, a fixer with edit rights, a read-only verifier), invoked strictly one after another by the main agent, each handed the previous one's returned report. Keep them serial and unisolated, since all three must see the same working tree.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Agent team of three specialists. It loses on the two things this need has: teams are the wrong tool for sequential work with heavy dependencies, and they do not isolate teammates in worktrees, so three peers in the same handful of hot files overwrite each other.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. The main agent decides when each stage runs and what it forwards, so the strict ordering is judgment, not a guarantee; the harness only enforces each subagent's tool allowlist and its context isolation. If the ordering genuinely must not drift, that is the argument for lifting it into a workflow script.
sheets.context_boundary: Three separate context windows within one session. Each stage receives only its spawn prompt plus whatever the previous stage's summary contained, and returns a summary; the actual code changes cross between stages through the working tree rather than through context.
sheets.lifecycle: Each subagent starts when the main agent delegates to it and ends when it returns; the chain ends when the verifier reports. Nothing survives the turn, and an interruption restarts the delegating turn rather than resuming a stage.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory and lossy at the seams: the fixer only knows what the finder's summary carried, so a thin summary silently drops findings, and nothing forces the verifier to actually rerun the measurement rather than reasoning about the diff. Because all three touch the same hot files, any accidental overlap or parallelism corrupts the edits, which is why the documented remedy (worktree isolation) is unavailable here.
sheets.version_caveat: Subagents are stable with no experimental flag, enabling env var or plan restriction, and this chain needs none. The confirmed version note is that /agents stopped opening a panel at v2.1.198 and now just prints the subagent file locations; promoting the three specialists to teammates instead would move the design onto the experimental, env-gated agent teams path.

sheets.primary: Subagents invoked in sequence from a single session: a performance-analysis subagent, then a fix subagent, then a verification subagent, with the main agent passing each one's returned result into the next one's prompt. Package the ordering as a skill or slash command so the sequence is stated once and reused.
sheets.rejected_alternative: An agent team. Rejected because teammates are concurrent peers with no worktree isolation, and three of them working the same handful of hot files would overwrite each other; the documented guidance is that sequential work, same-file edits and dependency-heavy chains belong in a single session with subagents rather than a team.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. Nothing in the harness makes step two wait for step one or forces step three to happen at all; the main agent chooses the order. The harness only enforces each subagent's tool allowlist and context isolation, and hooks (PostToolUse or Stop) are the only way to make a missing verification step actually block.
sheets.context_boundary: Each specialist runs in its own context window and returns only a summary, which becomes the next specialist's input. The exploration behind the performance findings never reaches the fixer, and the fixer's raw diff reasoning never reaches the verifier; the shared files on disk are the other channel between them.
sheets.lifecycle: The chain starts when you make the request or run the command, each subagent ends when it returns, and the sequence is over once the verifier reports. It has no standing effect afterwards, and each rerun re-derives everything from scratch.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open. The main agent can skip the verifier, re-analyse instead of consuming what it was handed, or fix things that were never on the analyser's list, and the summary-only handoff is lossy, so exact file and line detail the fixer needs can be dropped. If the strict ordering genuinely has to be guaranteed, that is the argument for moving these three steps into a workflow script.
sheets.version_caveat: Subagents are generally available with no flag, plan gate or experimental status; definitions load from project, user, plugin or CLI-defined scope. `/agents` stopped opening a panel in v2.1.198 and now just points at the definition files. If the lossy handoff hurts, a forked subagent started with `/subtask` inherits the full conversation instead of starting fresh.

scenarios.scenario: Before committing to a design for a new developer tool, I want it explored from three angles at once, user experience, technical architecture, and a devil's advocate, with the perspectives reacting to each other's arguments as they form, and I want to jump into any one explorer mid-flight and redirect it.

key.primary: Agent team: three teammates with distinct perspectives who message each other directly, each a full session the user can open and steer while it works
key.rejected_alternative: A dynamic workflow that drafts the design from several independent angles and weighs them
key.rejection_reason: Workflows explicitly support drafting a plan from several angles and weighing them against each other, which makes this the near-miss, but workflow agents never converse and the run accepts no mid-run user input, so neither the live cross-perspective argument nor the mid-flight redirection is possible. This three-perspective exploration with a devil's advocate is the team docs' own first-team example, and direct teammate interaction is the capability teams uniquely add.
key.lifecycle: explicit spawn request describing the three roles; requires the experimental env flag at session start
key.failure_mode: An unattended team drifts and wastes effort (docs: monitor and steer, letting a team run too long unattended increases wasted work); the lead may synthesize before teammates finish and must sometimes be told to wait.
key.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default; requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1

sheets.primary: An agent team of three teammates, one on user experience, one on technical architecture and one playing devil's advocate, spawned from a single natural-language instruction to the lead, which populates the shared task list and synthesizes findings at the end. This is the documented starter example for agent teams, and teammates message each other directly so the perspectives react as they form.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Subagents. They report only to the main agent, never message each other, and cannot be opened mid-run and redirected, so neither the cross-talk between perspectives nor your ability to steer one explorer would exist.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. The lead spawns the explorers, routes the discussion and decides when the exploration is done; you influence it through the spawn prompt and by messaging teammates. Hooks on TaskCreated, TaskCompleted and TeammateIdle are the only harness-side gate, for example to keep an explorer working when it goes idle too early.
sheets.context_boundary: Each explorer is an independent session with its own context window, loading CLAUDE.md, MCP servers and skills plus the lead's spawn prompt, without the lead's conversation history. Arguments cross as mailbox messages between named teammates and as shared task-list state; when you open a teammate, your typed text and skills go to it while built-in commands still run in the lead's session.
sheets.lifecycle: The team exists from the first spawn until the session ends, one team per session with no nesting and no promoting a teammate to lead. You redirect an explorer by selecting it in the agent panel and pressing Enter, interrupt with Escape, stop it with 'x', or ask the lead to have it shut down, which the teammate may reject.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open in ways that specifically bite the jump-in requirement: Claude may spawn subagents instead of forming a team and the agent panel alone does not confirm which happened, so you have to ask again and explicitly request a team. Idle rows hide after 30 seconds and surplus idle rows collapse into one counted row, which makes an explorer look gone when it is still running and addressable, and three parallel sessions cost significantly more tokens than one.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental and off by default until CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 is set. Teammates do not inherit the lead's /model unless you set Default teammate model in /config, and their model and fast mode are fixed at spawn; as of v2.1.199 typing /model while viewing a teammate warns that it applies to the lead, and idle-row behaviour differs across v2.1.181 through v2.1.199.

sheets.primary: Agent team of three teammates, one on user experience, one on technical architecture and one playing devil's advocate, spawned by the lead and messaging each other as their arguments form. You steer any one of them directly from the agent panel: arrow keys to select, Enter to open that teammate's transcript and type to it, Escape to interrupt its current turn, or click into its pane in split-pane mode.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Dynamic workflow drafting the design from several independent angles. It loses on both live requirements: workflow agents cannot react to each other while running, and a run accepts no mid-run user input, so jumping into one explorer to redirect it is impossible by construction.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. The lead is a Claude session that decides decomposition and synthesis, and nothing harness-side makes the devil's advocate actually dissent or makes the other two respond to it; the shared task list and the team hooks are the only mechanical parts.
sheets.context_boundary: Three independent sessions, each with its own context window, each loading project context (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) plus its spawn prompt but not the lead's conversation history. Peer messages, shared task-list state, your direct messages to a selected teammate, and the lead's final synthesis are what cross.
sheets.lifecycle: The team forms at the first spawn once the experimental flag is set and you confirm, and lasts until the teammates shut down or the session exits, which cleans up the team config directory automatically. Idle teammate rows hide from the panel about 30 seconds after everything goes idle, but the teammate is still running and addressable by name.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory, and the specific trap is that Claude may spawn plain subagents instead of forming a team; the agent panel looks the same either way, and with subagents there is no cross-talk and no way to drop into one, so ask again and request a team explicitly. Teammates can also stop on errors instead of recovering, and the lead may synthesize before the exploration is really finished.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default; requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, on the v2.1.178 or later implicit lifecycle. Mid-flight intervention depends on display mode: in-process is the default since v2.1.179, split panes need tmux or iTerm2 (explicit "iterm2" mode with the it2 CLI from v2.1.186) and are unsupported in VS Code's terminal, Windows Terminal and Ghostty; idle-row panel behaviour changed at v2.1.199.

sheets.primary: An agent team: ask the lead to spawn three teammates, one on user experience, one on technical architecture, one as devil's advocate, and to have them message each other as their arguments form. You attach to any explorer from the agent panel (arrow keys to select, Enter to open its transcript and type to it) and redirect it directly, or press Escape to interrupt its current turn.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A dynamic workflow. A workflow can draft a plan from several independent angles and weigh them against each other, but its runtime forbids mid-run user input and there is no individual agent to attach to, so 'jump into one explorer and redirect it' is exactly what it cannot do.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. The lead decides the split, the spawn prompts and when to synthesise; each teammate decides what it says to the others and whether it actually engages with the counter-arguments. The harness contributes the mailbox, the task list, the attach-and-message panel and interrupt keys.
sheets.context_boundary: Three independent full sessions plus the lead, each loading CLAUDE.md, MCP servers and skills but none of the lead's history. What crosses is the spawn prompt, teammate-to-teammate messages, your typed redirections while attached, idle notifications back to the lead, and any design document they write to disk. While viewing a teammate, plain text and skills go to it while built-in commands still run in the lead.
sheets.lifecycle: Begins when you approve the spawn, runs until the explorers are asked to shut down or the session ends. Idle teammate rows hide from the panel after about 30 seconds but the teammate is still running and addressable by name; the team directory is cleaned up on session exit.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open. The devil's advocate role is only a prompt, so it can drift into agreement; the lead may synthesise before the perspectives have actually collided; and unless you explicitly ask for a written artifact the whole exploration evaporates with the session. Cost is roughly three independent sessions plus coordination overhead.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental, disabled unless `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` is set. Panel behaviour is version sensitive: idle rows are not hidden before v2.1.181, hide per-teammate in v2.1.181 through v2.1.198, and only hide once the whole panel is idle from v2.1.199 (which also warns that `/model` typed at a teammate applies to the lead). Split-pane display needs tmux or iTerm2 with `it2` (explicit `iterm2` mode from v2.1.186).

sheets.primary: An agent team of three teammates with distinct charters (user experience, technical architecture, devil's advocate) sharing a channel so each reacts to the others' arguments while they are still forming, with every teammate individually addressable so you can jump in and redirect one mid-flight.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A brainstorming skill run in a single main context that role plays the three perspectives in turn. Rejected because one context blends the voices into a single house style and there is no separate explorer to jump into or redirect.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. Nothing forces the devil's advocate to be genuinely adversarial, and nothing forces the other two to update in response. The harness only guarantees that the three are separate and reachable.
sheets.context_boundary: Three context windows plus the shared channel. Arguments and any design document the teammates write cross that boundary; your main conversation receives the synthesis rather than three full exploration transcripts, and a redirect you send enters only the addressed teammate's window.
sheets.lifecycle: Lives for the exploration and ends when you settle the design or dissolve the team. It applies only before the commitment point and has no bearing on the implementation that follows unless a written artifact is produced deliberately.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open and is purely advisory. The dominant failure is convergence: three instances of the same model share priors and tend to agree, so the devil's advocate needs an explicit adversarial charter and will still soften over time. A second failure is producing no durable artifact, leaving the reasoning stranded in ephemeral team contexts.
sheets.version_caveat: Same caveat as the other team answers: this is the newest mechanism of the set, I believe it is opt-in or experimental, and I do not know the introducing version, the enabling flag, or whether it is restricted by plan.

scenarios.scenario: A review pass over recent changes should dispatch an independent verifier for each finding it produces, typically 5 to 10 findings, and none of the per-finding verification chatter should ever reach my conversation. I want exactly one final verified summary back.

key.primary: One subagent that spawns nested subagents: the reviewer delegates a verifier per finding and only the top-level summary returns to the session
key.rejected_alternative: A dynamic workflow with a review stage and a verify stage
key.rejection_reason: The fan-out is real but small and hangs entirely off one delegated task. The subagent docs name this exact shape as what nesting is for: 'a reviewer subagent that dispatches a verifier per finding, so the intermediate output never reaches your main conversation', with subagents able to spawn up to three layers below the main conversation by default. At 5 to 10 agents the workflow's launch approval, background runtime, and generated script buy nothing; workflows are for jobs that outgrow a handful of subagents.
key.context_boundary: isolated context (a nested subagent tree; intermediate results are confined to it and only the top-level summary returns)
key.lifecycle: model-decided delegation; nesting occurs inside the reviewer subagent when its tool list includes Agent and depth allows
key.failure_mode: At the depth limit the Agent tool is withheld and the leaf agent does the verification itself; verifier detail is only as visible as the reviewer's synthesis, so a weak summary hides verified evidence; every spawn counts against the 200-per-session subagent cap.
key.version_caveat: Nesting depth defaults to three layers as of v2.1.219, configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (v2.1.217+); v2.1.217 to v2.1.218 defaulted to one layer, and v2.1.172 to v2.1.216 allowed five

sheets.primary: A dynamic workflow: one phase reviews the recent changes and returns structured findings, a second phase dispatches one independent verifier agent per finding, and a final phase returns a single verified summary. Workflows exist precisely to apply this repeatable quality pattern, having independent agents cross-check findings before they are reported.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Subagent fan-out from the main conversation. Subagent results return to the caller's context window, so 5 to 10 verification summaries would land in your session and Claude would stitch them together turn by turn, which is exactly the chatter you ruled out.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The runtime executes the script, so the per-finding dispatch and the single merged return are control flow; Claude's context receives only the value the script returns. What each verifier concludes is still model judgment.
sheets.context_boundary: The script runs in an isolated environment separate from your conversation, and each verifier has its own context window whose result lives in a script variable. The only thing crossing into your session is the one final summary, plus the script path the runtime writes under your session directory in ~/.claude/projects/.
sheets.lifecycle: It starts on invocation, by asking for a workflow, using the ultracode keyword, or running a saved command, and runs in the background with phases visible in /workflows. It ends when the script returns its summary or when you stop it with 'x', and it is resumable only within the same session.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on verification semantics. A verifier that cannot check a finding, for example after a rate limit or API error, has to be handled deliberately: the bundled /deep-research reports such a claim as unverified rather than refuted as of v2.1.196, and a workflow that does not do the same will either drop or silently pass an unchecked finding into the one summary you see. Because there is no mid-run input, you cannot intervene while it happens.
sheets.version_caveat: Requires Claude Code v2.1.154 or later and a paid plan, with Pro enabling Dynamic workflows in /config; it can be turned off with disableWorkflows, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1, or org-wide managed settings. At 5 to 10 verifiers the run sits under the default medium size guideline of fewer than 15 agents, which has been the default since v2.1.219.

sheets.primary: Subagents used for verification fan-out: the review pass produces findings and dispatches one independent verifier subagent per finding, each investigating in its own window and returning only a verdict line with its evidence pointer, after which one merged verified summary is emitted.
sheets.rejected_alternative: An agent team of verifiers. Rejected on the scenario's own terms: independence between verifiers is the point, and team chatter is exactly the traffic that must not reach the conversation.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split. The harness owns the context isolation, so a verifier's tool calls and reasoning structurally cannot enter your window. The model owns whether it emits only the final summary and whether it honestly applies a negative verdict rather than reporting the finding anyway.
sheets.context_boundary: Each verifier's investigation stays in its own context; a short verdict crosses. Note the distinction the requirement turns on: if the review pass runs in your main conversation, you will see the dispatch calls themselves even though you never see their contents. Hiding the dispatches too requires the whole pass to run one level down.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs per review pass and ends with the single summary. Nothing standing, no persistence between passes, and it is not a gate on commit or merge unless something else makes it one.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open. Verifier independence is only as strong as what each verifier is given: handed a finding statement and asked to check it, models confirm far more often than they refute, so the pass can become a rubber stamp. If a verifier receives the finding text but not the code, its verdict carries no information at all.
sheets.version_caveat: I believe subagents in Claude Code cannot themselves dispatch further subagents (the Task tool is not available inside a subagent), and I am not certain whether that limitation has been lifted. If it still holds, the fan-out must originate in the main session, so the verification content is hidden but the dispatch calls are not, and the requirement is met only in substance.

sheets.primary: A dynamic workflow: a review phase produces the findings, then `pipeline()` spawns one independent verifier `agent()` per finding, and the script returns a single merged summary of what survived. This is the same adversarial cross-check pattern the bundled `/deep-research` workflow uses, so ask for it as a workflow and save the script once the shape is right.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Subagents, one verifier per finding. Rejected because a subagent reports its result back into the conversation that spawned it, so 5 to 10 verifier returns would land in the working context window one after another, which is precisely the per-finding chatter to be kept out.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The runtime guarantees that every finding gets its own verifier and that intermediate verdicts stay in script variables rather than in a context window; the model owns whether each claim actually holds up.
sheets.context_boundary: The orchestration runs in an isolated runtime outside the conversation. Each verifier has its own context and sees only its finding, the verdicts accumulate as script state, and exactly one value, the final verified summary, crosses back into the session.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs on invocation of the workflow, in the background while the session stays responsive, and ends when the summary is returned. Progress is visible in `/workflows` if you want it, but it is not pushed into the transcript; saving the script makes the review repeatable per branch.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open, and in a specific way: verification is model checking model, and when a verifier cannot check a claim (rate limit, API error) the claim is reported as unverified rather than refuted, so unchecked material still reaches your summary looking much like verified material. It is worth reading the unverified bucket rather than trusting the headline.
sheets.version_caveat: Requires v2.1.154 or later and a paid plan (Pro enables Dynamic workflows in `/config`); organisations can disable them entirely. The treatment of uncheckable claims as unverified rather than refuted is v2.1.196 or later, so on earlier versions genuine findings could be dropped. At 5 to 10 agents the run sits below the 25-agent large-workflow warning but may exceed a `small` size guideline.

sheets.primary: Dynamic workflow: a first stage agent produces the findings against a JSON schema, pipeline() spawns one independent verifier per finding, and a final agent merges the survivors into a single report. This is the cross-check pattern the bundled /deep-research workflow uses, applied to a diff instead of to sources.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Nested subagents, a reviewer subagent that spawns a verifier subagent per finding. It loses because the fan-out count and the decision to verify at all remain the model's turn-by-turn judgment, and subagent nesting is depth-limited, whereas a workflow keeps every verification exchange in script variables by construction.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The runtime executes the script, so 'one independent verifier per finding' is a loop over the findings array rather than an intention, and the isolation of the verification chatter is a property of the runtime rather than of the model's discretion about what to report.
sheets.context_boundary: Everything runs in the workflow runtime, isolated from your conversation: each verifier has its own context window and its output lands in a script variable. Only the final merged summary crosses into your context, which is exactly the requirement that none of the per-finding chatter reaches you.
sheets.lifecycle: It starts on an explicit workflow invocation (a saved /<name>, or the 'use a workflow'/ultracode opt-in) and runs in the background while your session stays responsive, ending when the script returns its one summary. Resume works within the same session; exiting Claude Code makes the next session start fresh.
sheets.failure_mode: The failures are silent by design here, because you only ever see the summary: a verifier that dies resolves to null, so a finding can be dropped or logged as unverified rather than refuted, and a shrinking report looks like a clean bill of health rather than a broken verification stage. There is no mid-run input either, so a verifier that needs clarification cannot ask; it can only be stopped from /workflows.
sheets.version_caveat: Requires Claude Code v2.1.154 or later, on any paid plan (Pro must enable it from the Dynamic workflows row in /config), the Anthropic API, Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry. The unverified-versus-refuted distinction in the bundled cross-check report dates from v2.1.196; before that an unchecked claim counted as refuted.
